glossary.fixedCharge.def: What you pay each month just for being connected, even with zero consumption.
glossary.igv.def: Tax added at the end, on energy plus the fixed charge. You can turn it off here to see the net amount.
glossary.lighting.def: Share for street lights. Separate from your consumption and usually a small part of the bill.
glossary.kwh.def: One kilowatt-hour: running something at 1000 W for one hour.

explainer.title: From kWh to soles, step by step
explainer.intro: The calculator does not estimate by eye. Here is the whole sum, step by step, so you can redo it with your own bill.
explainer.inverse.title: Backwards: from soles to kWh
explainer.inverse.body: To estimate consumption from an amount, we undo the steps in reverse: first divide by 1 plus the IGV, then subtract the charges, and finally divide by the price. The order matters: IGV is undone before subtracting charges, because on the way in it taxes the whole subtotal. If the price is 0, or the amount doesn't even cover the charges with their IGV, the result is 0 kWh.
explainer.inverse.caption: The example total, converted back
explainer.toggles.title: The switches
explainer.toggles.body: Fixed charge, public lighting and VAT each have a switch in settings: turn one off and that component counts as 0. And a two-month period multiplies every component by 2 before totalling.
explainer.example.title: The sum, line by line
explainer.example.caption: VAT applies to the whole subtotal, not to each charge separately.
explainer.find.title: The four numbers, and where they are on your bill
explainer.find.body: Everything comes from four figures already printed on your bill. Find them once, write them down, and you can repeat the maths any month.
explainer.find.price.label: Price per kWh
explainer.find.price.where: The energy charge divided by the kWh billed; usually carries four decimals. It is the only component that depends on how much you use.
explainer.find.fixed.label: Fixed charge
explainer.find.fixed.where: Listed under that name, in soles. Billed for being connected to the grid, whether you use power or not.
explainer.find.lighting.label: Public lighting
explainer.find.lighting.where: Its own line, also in soles. It pays for the street lights, not the ones in your home.
explainer.find.igv.label: VAT (IGV)
explainer.find.igv.where: At the end, as tax on the subtotal. Energy and charges are taxed alike. The rate today is 18%.
explainer.formula.title: The whole formula
explainer.formula.caption: Everything else on this page is a variation of this single line.
explainer.diy.title: Check it against your bill
explainer.diy.s1: Multiply your billed kWh by your price per kWh, then add the fixed charge and public lighting.
explainer.diy.s3: Compare the result with the total printed on your bill.
explainer.diy.check: Matches within a few cents? Then your four numbers are right: load them into the calculator settings and you can project any consumption from there.
explainer.limits.title: What might not add up
explainer.limits.lighting: Public lighting. Treated here as a flat amount, but the regulation defines it as a share: it cannot exceed 5% of the total billed and is split across users by consumption bracket. If your consumption swings, this line moves.
explainer.limits.fose: FOSE. Low consumption can qualify for the Electric Social Compensation Fund discount, which this calculator does not model.
explainer.limits.rounding: Rounding. Every line is rounded to cents, so a few cents of difference against your bill is normal.
explainer.limits.tariff: Your tariff. The numbers on this page come from the only tariff verified against a real bill: BT5B residential, Lima Norte, June 2026. The calculator’s other tariffs are estimates, and the price per kWh varies by electrical system and is updated periodically.
explainer.sources.title: References
explainer.sources.intro: None of this has to be taken on trust: every part can be checked against the official source behind it.
